- **Probe.** Each Reconcile, after Sessions, run in the main checkout `node scripts/pilot-probe.mjs <main checkout> --apply --status --capacity {{repo}} --main {{main}} --handoff-after 2` [optional: plus the adapter's Pool section's `--skip-labels <label>,...`]. Act on its lines as `PILOT-STORE.md` and the `issue-pilot` skill describe: `WORKER <n> DONE <sha>` and `WORKER <n> STOP <cause>` results are written back by `--apply`; `STAGEABLE <key>` goes to Stage; `HELD <n> G<k>` waits for that gate (stage nothing in that batch); `MOVE`, `PARKED`, `UNPARK` go to Batch (a `MOVE` that lists `done` members moves those out, without `--state stop`); `UNPARK_FRESH <n>` (a member parked with `--fresh`) goes straight to the fresh redispatch with `<n>` as the key, without `unpark` or Stage first; `UNBLOCKED <key> <n>` means a stopped member's blockers are all closed, so redispatch it fresh when its stop was waiting on them, ahead of the `PARKED` handling for that member; `IN_MAIN <key>` goes to Close; `RESUME_PUSH` and `NOT_IN_MAIN` go to the Push gate; `OVERLAP` lines are reported, not filtered; `CONFLICT <key> <n> <m|integration> <file…>` (right after `STAGEABLE <key>`) names the files a real merge of that pair conflicts on: a forecast that changes nothing about Stage (the Stage command still resolves what it can and stops on the rest, whose handling needs its source and kind fields), reported so no new work touching those files is dispatched before the pair is settled; `BUDGET <file> <total> <limit> <n…>` means those members together push `<file>` past its size budget though each fits alone: handle it before Pick, have a running member's worker put the new text in the split file the pointer names, and move a `done` member out before Stage; `REQUEST`, `GATE` and `HOLD` are handled before Pick; `POOL_READY` means run the Pool command; `POOL_TRIAGE` means refine those `needs-triage` Issues per Pool, which makes the tick not idle; `HUMAN_NO_GATE <n> <summary>` is a `ready-for-human` Issue no open gate asks about: open one with the Gates command (`--issue #<n>`, the question from the summary, the most conservative option as default) and ask it in this tick's Report with `AskUserQuestion`; `ADAPTER_AHEAD` lines end with ` ｜ ` and the command that saves the adapter ref's copy (the integration branch, or the Pilot **Adapter ref** entry's ref, fetched first when remote) under `<main checkout>/.scratch/pilot/adapter/`: run it and Read the saved file instead of a diff or printed `git show` output; `SCRIPT_AHEAD <path> run-in <stage worktree>` (printed with `ADAPTER_AHEAD`) names a `scripts/` file that adapter names and the main checkout lacks or holds an older copy of: run it as `<stage worktree>/<path>` from the main checkout this tick, since an old copy can fail silently (a watcher reading only the last `--batch`); `SCRIPT_AHEAD <path> sync-main` means the stage worktree lacks it too, so run Integration branch's `sync-main` first; `HOOK_BEHIND <path>` names a script a `.claude/settings.json` hook runs whose main-checkout copy is behind `pilot/integration`: when that hook blocks or fails, reproduce with `git -C <main checkout> show pilot/integration:<path>` before reporting it, and drop it when that version passes; `HUMAN_LANDED <n> <sha>` is a `ready-for-human` Issue whose work already landed on `pilot/integration`: read its last comment and that commit before asking the human, never ask them to run a step that already ran, and name the SHA in this tick's Report (and in the gate's question when `HUMAN_NO_GATE` lists it too); `BLOCKER_OPEN_SCOPE <n> #<m> <label>` means blocker `#m` landed on `pilot/integration` but still carries `<label>` and is unassigned or had its body edited after its last assignment, so `#n` is not dispatchable (when `#m` is assigned and its edit history shows the last edit was the coordinator's own, such as a `COUNTERPART_BARE` rewrite before Close, ignore the line and open nothing): only `#m`'s old scope is done; when `#m` is assigned it closes with its batch, so open a new Issue for the rewritten scope and make `#n` blocked by it; `SCOPE_CHANGED <key> <n> <edited at>` means a `done` member's Issue body was edited after its worker started: read what changed before Stage; when the edit history shows the last edit was the coordinator's own (such as a `COUNTERPART_BARE` rewrite), ignore the line and open nothing; otherwise open a new Issue for scope the candidate lacks, blocked by this one, and add it as a blocker of the Issues waiting on this one; neither line blocks Stage. `WORKER <n> STUCK …` goes to the human and `WORKER <n> RUNNING <minutes>` needs nothing; the always-printed `HANDOFF_COUNT <n>/<threshold>` and `HANDOFF_DUE` follow the adapter's handoff condition; the other lines (`NOT_MAIN`, `DIRTY`, `SETTINGS_INVALID`, `ADAPTER_AHEAD_SEEN`, `DEPS_PROSE`, `DEPS_PROSE_FAILED`, `POOL_EMPTY`, `POOL_FAILED`, `PARENT_LABEL`, `PARENT_REOPEN`, `PARENT_APPLY_FAILED`, `APPLY_MISS`, `RESTAGE`, `REGRESSING`, `FETCH_FAILED`, `PUSH_PARKED`, `MAIN_PAUSED`, `BEHIND_MAIN`, `OVER_CAP`) are handled as `PILOT-STORE.md`'s `pilot-probe.mjs` row and the adapter's Probe lines say. An exit 3 with `CHECKPOINT_LOCKED` is a batch checkpoint lock timeout from `--apply` (that batch unwritten, the other lines valid): skip the Bare guard and rerun the same command once the lock holder ended. On any other non-zero exit, run the Bare guard by hand, report its stderr, and do not stage or merge this tick.
